items.title: Release Notes on a map!
items.content_html:
I’m enjoying using and building Release Notes so much I added some great location features today and polished up the user experience!

  • Notes can save where you are with one tap, and name the café or park you’re in
  • iPhone photos bring their place and time with them, HEIC included
  • Notes without a place of their own show that day’s city
  • A new Map page shows every note with a place, filtered by words, tag or release
  • Place links in notes and emails open on Release Notes’ own map
  • A design pass across every page: You, Settings, Activity, Badges, Pause, Delete and Connect
  • Every email polished to match, with dark mode for the account emails

If you are looking for a journaling experience that is similar to what I’m looking for — you can sign up and use it too!

It make me irrationally annoyed when the junk drawer has toothpicks all over the place. Printed this little box and problem solved!
Red leaves. 🍂

Melting wax to pour some candles. I’ve made over a thousand candles at this point but because we only do it once a year I always feel like I have no idea what I’m doing when we start pouring. Good thing I learned to keep good notes with weights! Let the candle making begin!

After flipping to my own custom theme for my blog I was able to ship something I’ve wanted for a very long time: all of my personal sites are now connected with a navigation header at the very top of the page. For the first time it is easy to jump from site to site!

items.title: Phishing Fear
items.content_html:
Well done phishing campaign just landed in my inbox. This one gave me a pause and smartly goes after a “fear” motive. Did someone just compromise my account? That anxiety could lead to a quick login attempt and complete takeover. The info@rumpunch.io from address was easy to spot though. The other mistake was the “New York” with a Norway flag. Also seems their link was taken down with a 404.

jamie ~ % curl --head 'https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/securemai.custredir91224.com%2F[…]'
HTTP/2 404 
server: awselb/2.0
date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 16:18:48 GMT
content-type: application/text
content-length: 0
x-robots-tag: noindex

Stay safe out there! 🤞

items.title: Release Notes gets Badges
items.content_html:
I decided to have some fun and I added badges to my Your Version Number: Release Notes project.

Some specifics on how they work:

  • Your birthday is a release and every day is a patch, so badges speak release engineering, with tiers from alpha through beta, rc and stable to LTS.
  • Four tracks reward consistency, not perfection: days in a row, steady weeks, total days with notes, and how much of each year of life you cover.
  • Firsts point you at features you might not know about, like replying to the email, adding a voice memo or filling in a day you missed.
  • Collectibles live in the version number itself: round numbers, palindromes, your birthday, and a few secret ones.
  • Every birthday starts a new album, so there’s always something new to collect.
  • Nothing is ever taken away. A missed day is never called out, and there are no points, leaderboards or “at risk” warnings.
  • If badges aren’t your thing, one “Show badges” setting turns them all off.

I didn’t know that I would have so much fun building my own journaling app! 🤩

I added a new Upcoming feature to Release Notes:

Release Notes now has a new section for what’s coming next. In Upcoming you can save birthdays, anniversaries, trips, and one-time events. You can choose when you would like these events to show up in your Release Notes. Trips include a destination with a start and end date. All of these upcoming events are private to only you.

I’m having a lot of fun journaling each day’s version.

items.title: The nnxyz rooms
items.content_html:
Years ago I discovered the work of nnxyz on nifty.ink. I acquired a few of his pieces and grew to like it more and more. I ended up collecting four complete collections of hundreds of pieces. I had always wished to create a gallery like experience for anyone to experience. With the help of AI I was able to make that vision a reality.

Check out the nnxyz rooms.

Some highlights of what the website has.

  • Every drawing can be watched being made. The 574 Nifty Ink works are rebuilt from their archived brush strokes as native vector images, and each one replays stroke by stroke, with the recorded order, widths, colors and transparency.
  • Hung like a museum, not a feed. Six wings, 28 rooms, 626 works. Every work hangs in exactly one room, rooms hold 20 to 30 works, and each room is hung in the order the works were drawn, so a walk through a room is a walk through a few weeks of drawing.
  • Wall text in a museum voice. Each room has an introduction, chapters, labels, one-line notes, explained comparisons and a closing.
  • An audio tour in every room. Press play and a voice reads the room while each work comes on screen, about seven minutes a room, with pause, skip and a progress line.
  • A screen saver that draws. One work at a time, drawn stroke by stroke on black, held with its caption, then the next. Fullscreen, with your choice of drawing speed and hold time, and it can be limited to one room.
  • A map of the building. The collection as a three-floor museum map, rooms sized by how many works they hold, colored by collection, with doors between consecutive rooms and stairs between floors.
  • Readable by machines too. /llms.txt indexes the site for language models and /llms-full.txt carries the complete gallery text in one file.
  • Light or dark. A white gallery by default, black by choice, remembered across visits. The artwork itself is never altered.
  • Everything downloadable. Each artwork page offers the native SVG, the original PNG and the archived metadata and provenance records, with a link to the collected NFT.

I hope you like browsing and experiencing nnxyz’s work as much as I do. I feel like it has real movement and energy in it. nnxyz himself uses the term “thrash-art” — I dig it! I’ve never liked the VR gallery experiences online and I think this museum walk through, particularly with audio guidance, is a better way to experience it.

We saw Sting tonight at the Orpheum. It was really cool to see a music legend in such a small venue. It was a great show including a wide range of his catalog. According to Wikipedia he is 75 years old but doesn’t seem like it!

Years ago I purchased three collections of art by nnxyz on nifty.ink. I’ve now archived them in better detail than they were ever before available on my nnxyz collection site. Nifty.ink captured all art in dots and strokes so I used that to render SVG versions of all the art. Lovely. 🎨
